title: Casual Leave
content: Every employee receives 12 days of casual leave per calendar year, credited in full on January 1 (pro-rated in your first year). Casual leave is for short, unplanned needs and may be taken in half-day units. Unused casual leave lapses on December 31 and is not carried forward or encashed.

title: Earned Leave
content: Earned leave, also called annual leave, accrues at 1.5 days per month, giving 18 days per year. It can be used only after probation is confirmed. Requests for three or more consecutive days need at least five working days' notice and your manager's approval in the Employee Self-Service portal.

title: Public Holidays
content: BuzzTech observes 12 fixed public holidays each year, published by People Operations in December for the coming year. In addition, every employee has two floating holidays to use for personal or regional festivals; floating holidays must be requested at least one week ahead and cannot be carried forward.

title: Maternity Leave
content: Eligible employees receive 26 weeks of paid maternity leave. Leave may start up to four weeks before the expected delivery date. Notify People Operations at least eight weeks before your expected leave start so that your cover and benefits can be arranged. Employees who have not completed probation should speak to People Operations about their options.

title: Bereavement and Marriage Leave
content: Employees receive five paid days of bereavement leave on the death of an immediate family member, and five paid days of marriage leave on their own marriage. Both can be taken in a single block, and neither reduces your casual, sick, or earned leave balance. Inform your manager and People Operations as soon as you can.

title: Hybrid Work Policy
content: BuzzTech follows a hybrid model: employees work in the office three days a week, Tuesday to Thursday, and may work from home on Monday and Friday. Roles that require lab or hardware access may have different in-office days, which your manager will confirm. Team events and onboarding sessions take priority over remote days.

title: Working From Home for an Extended Period
content: If you need to work remotely for more than five consecutive working days outside the normal hybrid pattern, get written approval from your manager and notify People Operations. Working from another country is not allowed without prior approval from People Operations, because it can affect tax and legal obligations. Requests should be made at least two weeks in advance.

title: Submitting Expense Reimbursements
content: Submit business expense claims in the expense tool within 30 days of the expense. Attach an itemised receipt for any expense above 10 USD, and select the project or cost centre. Approved claims are paid with the next payroll if approved before the 20th, and with the following month's payroll otherwise.

title: Client Meals and Team Events
content: Meals with clients are reimbursed up to 25 USD per person with prior manager approval, and the receipt must list all attendees. Team events are funded from the department budget and need the department head's approval before booking. Alcohol is not reimbursable under any category.

title: Conflicts of Interest and Gifts
content: Disclose any outside business interest, second job, or family relationship that could affect your work to your manager and People Operations. Gifts from clients or suppliers worth more than 50 USD must be declined or reported, and cash gifts are never acceptable. Failure to disclose a conflict of interest can lead to disciplinary action.

title: Social Media Use
content: You may use social media in a personal capacity, but you must not share confidential information, speak on behalf of BuzzTech without authorisation, or post content that harasses or discriminates against others. If you identify yourself as a BuzzTech employee, make it clear that your views are your own.

title: Reporting Harassment and the Investigation Process
content: Report harassment to People Operations, your manager, or the confidential ethics line, which is open 24 hours and can be used anonymously. The Internal Committee acknowledges every report within two working days and aims to complete its investigation within 30 days. Both parties are heard, and the findings are shared with them in writing.

title: Performance Review Cycle
content: BuzzTech runs two review cycles a year. The mid-year check-in takes place in July and is a development conversation without a rating. The annual review takes place in January and includes a self-assessment, manager assessment, and a final rating. Goals are set in April for the new cycle, and your manager discusses your rating with you in a one-to-one meeting.

title: Performance Improvement Plan
content: If your performance is below expectations, your manager may place you on a 60-day Performance Improvement Plan with clear goals and weekly check-ins. People Operations is informed and you can ask for support or training. If the goals are met, the plan ends; if they are not, further action may follow, including termination.

title: Raising a Workplace Grievance
content: If you have a concern about your treatment at work that is not covered by another policy, first try to resolve it with your manager. If that is not possible, raise it with People Operations in writing. People Operations will respond within five working days and meet you within ten working days. You may bring a colleague to the meeting for support.

title: Documents to Bring on Your First Day
content: Bring one government-issued photo ID, proof of your address, your signed offer letter, your bank account details for payroll, and your tax identification number. If you worked elsewhere before, also bring your last relieving letter and most recent payslip. People Operations will not be able to activate your payroll record until the bank details and tax number are submitted.

title: Laptop Setup and First Login
content: The IT Service Desk pre-installs your laptop with the standard BuzzTech image, which includes the VPN client, the collaboration suite, and disk encryption. On first login you must change your temporary password and enroll in multi-factor authentication. You should complete both steps before leaving the IT Service Desk so that support staff can help if anything fails.

title: Adding Dependants to Your Health Insurance
content: You can add your spouse and up to three children to the group health insurance during your enrollment window. You will need to upload a marriage certificate or birth certificate for each dependant. Dependants added after the 30-day window require a qualifying life event and must be submitted to People Operations within 30 days of that event.

title: Probation Period
content: All new employees serve a probation period of three months. Your manager holds check-ins at 30, 60, and 80 days and records a written confirmation decision before the period ends. Probation can be extended once, by up to three months, if more time is needed to assess performance. During probation, either party may end employment with 15 days' written notice.

title: Mandatory Training for New Hires
content: Within your first two weeks you must complete four mandatory online modules: Information Security Basics, Code of Conduct, Anti-Harassment and Respect at Work, and Data Privacy. Each module takes about 30 minutes and ends with a short quiz that requires 80 percent to pass. Completion is tracked in the learning portal, and your manager is notified if modules are overdue.

title: Who to Contact During Onboarding
content: For questions about contracts, benefits, or documents, contact People Operations. For laptop, accounts, and access problems, contact the IT Service Desk. For questions about your role and first-week plan, ask your manager or your buddy. If you cannot find an answer in this assistant, you can ask it to raise a support ticket on your behalf.

title: Accessing Your Payslip
content: Your payslip is published in the Employee Self-Service portal on the day salary is paid. You can view and download payslips for the past 36 months, and annual tax summaries for the past five years. Payslips are not sent by email, to protect your personal information.

title: Annual Tax Declaration
content: Every employee submits a tax declaration once a year in January through the Employee Self-Service portal, listing planned investments and eligible deductions. Payroll uses the declaration to calculate monthly tax withholding for the rest of the financial year. A final proof submission window opens in February, when you upload supporting documents; unverified declarations are removed and any extra tax is deducted from the March salary.

title: Changing Your Bank Account
content: To change your bank account, submit the new details and a cancelled cheque or bank statement in the Employee Self-Service portal. The change takes five business days to verify. If you submit it after the 20th of the month, your next salary may still go to the old account, so submit changes early.

title: Annual Salary Revision
content: Salary revisions take effect on April 1 and are based on the annual performance review rating and market benchmarks. Employees receive their revision letters in late March. Employees who joined after October 1 become eligible for revision in the following cycle.

title: Exercising Vested Stock Options
content: You can exercise vested options during the two exercise windows each year, in May and in November. You pay the exercise price per share plus applicable taxes, and shares are credited to your equity account within ten business days. Options that have not vested are cancelled when your employment ends.

title: Salary Advance
content: Confirmed employees can request one emergency salary advance per year of up to one month's base pay. Requests are made to People Operations with your manager's approval and are recovered in up to six equal monthly deductions. Advances are not available during probation or the notice period.

title: Final Settlement When You Leave
content: Your final settlement includes salary up to your last working day, encashment of unused earned leave, and any pending expense claims, less recoveries such as unreturned equipment or unserved notice. It is paid within 45 days of your last working day, after the exit clearance process is complete. You will receive a settlement statement and your experience letter on the same day.
